m6-t1.question: What is the test that separates a decision metric from a vanity metric?
options: Whether the number is large or small
Whether knowing it would change what we do next
Whether the platform highlights it on the home screen
Whether it can be shown as a chart
m6-t1.explanation: Reach, impressions and followers feel good and answer no question — if no action changes, it is decoration.

m6-t1.question: In the KPI tree, what sits between the business goal and the diagnostics?
options: Vanity metrics
Channel KPIs like enquiries per channel and the conversion rate
The ad budget
Follower counts per platform
m6-t1.explanation: Goal → KPIs → channel KPIs → diagnostics: the tree shows where money and effort convert and which branch is thin.

m6-t1.question: A report says 'form conversion 12%'. What two companions make this number meaningful?
options: The ad spend and the bounce rate
The baseline (it was 8% last month) and a benchmark (category range 6–10%)
The page speed score and word count
The number of likes on the post
m6-t1.explanation: Your own before and the industry's typical turn a bare number into a sentence with direction.

m6-t1.question: In the weekly insight ritual, how many anomalies should you chase?
options: All of them, to be thorough
One — the number that moved most, up or down
Three, spread across channels
None — just record the numbers
m6-t1.explanation: Find the one anomaly, diagnose with the tree's diagnostics, decide one action with an owner and date, and log it.

m6-t1.question: Why is the insight log called the secret weapon?
options: It hides underperforming channels from the client
After a quarter it becomes a narrative of what worked — portfolio and interview material
It replaces the need for GA4
It guarantees budget increases
m6-t1.explanation: The log records what moved, why, and what you did — a quarter later it is exactly the story employers ask for.

m6-t2.question: What is the core unit of measurement in GA4?
options: The visit
The event — an action with parameters (which page, which link, what value)
The bounce
The impression
m6-t2.explanation: GA4 counts events; users, sessions and page views are aggregations of events, not separate categories.

m6-t2.question: What is the rule about unverified GA4 installations?
options: They work fine after 48 hours automatically
An unverified installation does not exist — confirm in Realtime/DebugView
Google emails you when the tag fires
Verification is only needed for e-commerce
m6-t2.explanation: Verify with DebugView or the Realtime report; a typo'd ID or wrong property is invisible until you look.

m6-t2.question: In Traffic acquisition, which source/medium row represents Google Ads traffic?
options: google / organic
l.google (paid) — alongside cpc bidding
(direct) / (none)
instagram.com / referral
m6-t2.explanation: Organic is google/organic; paid search arrives as l.google with cpc; social arrives as referral from the platform.

m6-t2.question: If you configure only ONE thing in a new GA4 property, what should it be?
options: Forty conversions, to be thorough
One key event that proxies the business action — enquiry, WhatsApp start, or booking
Page views as conversions
A custom dimension for weather
m6-t2.explanation: One business-proxy conversion first; then link Search Console and Ads; leave enhanced measurement on.

m6-t2.question: Why should GA4 numbers be quoted with a little humility?
options: GA4 is known to double-count everything
Consent mode, sampling in explorations, and modelled attribution make the edges soft — say 'about'
Google rounds all numbers up
Only paid accounts get accurate data
m6-t2.explanation: GA4 numbers are the best available estimate, not an audit — treat them as decision-grade, not accounting-grade.

m6-t3.question: What is 'the manual layer' in dashboard design?
options: The platform's data, entered by hand
The numbers no platform has — how-did-you-hear tallies, walk-ins, WhatsApp conversation counts — kept in a sheet
The PDF that is printed each month
A backup of the dashboard
m6-t3.explanation: Spreadsheets hold what no platform tracks; they are a first-class data source in Looker Studio, not a second-class citizen.

m6-t3.question: Which set describes the five panels of the stakeholder dashboard?
options: Logo, hero image, three photo galleries
Header KPIs with comparison, one trend line, channel breakdown, funnel, anomaly notes
Twenty charts covering every metric
A table of all raw events
m6-t3.explanation: The dashboard IS the KPI tree drawn live: KPIs, trend, channels, funnel, and notes that explain the numbers.

m6-t3.question: According to the lesson, what is the number-one source of broken dashboards?
options: Too few charts
Clever data blends — joining sources breaks silently; prefer side-by-side panels
Using the demo property
Sharing view access too widely
m6-t3.explanation: Blending two connectors on a shared dimension is fragile; adjacent panels deliver the same insight safely.

m6-t3.question: Which is the strongest form of automation for reporting?
options: A bigger server
Culture — the standing agenda item where the weekly ritual opens on the dashboard
Exporting to PDF manually each week
Emailing raw CSV files
m6-t3.explanation: Scheduled PDFs and alerts help, but the standing meeting ritual is the automation that cannot be uninstalled.

m6-t3.question: The audience principle says a report's job is to:
options: Demonstrate how hard the team worked
Provoke a decision or renew confidence — if a reader can do nothing with a panel, delete it
Include every metric for completeness
Look impressive to outsiders
m6-t3.explanation: Reports exist to be acted on; effort-display panels are posters, and posters get ignored.

m6-t4.question: Why did the home-bakery owner wrongly conclude 'Instagram brings no sales'?
options: She posted at the wrong times
Last-click attribution credited conversions to direct/WhatsApp, hiding Instagram's role as the discovery touch
Instagram deleted her analytics
Her reels were too short
m6-t4.explanation: The last touch gets all the credit; discovery channels that feed the funnel get starved — the most expensive reading mistake.

m6-t4.question: Which attribution model is GA4's default, using machine learning to distribute credit?
options: Last-click
Data-driven attribution (DDA)
First-click
Linear
m6-t4.explanation: DDA weights credit by which touch sequences actually precede conversion; know which model is speaking and never compare across models.

m6-t4.question: What question does attribution NOT answer, that incrementality does?
options: Which channel got credit?
Would it have happened anyway?
Which touch was last?
How many conversions occurred?
m6-t4.explanation: Attribution distributes credit for what happened; only incrementality checks (pause tests, geo splits, how-did-you-hear logs) reveal what the channel actually caused.

m6-t4.question: Which of these is NOT a valid A/B test?
options: Random 50/50 split of visitors between two headlines
Comparing last month's page (A) with this month's page (B)
Meta A/B test campaigns with automatic random assignment
Email subject line tests with randomised sends
m6-t4.explanation: Before-vs-after changed time too — seasonality, campaigns and luck ride along. Randomised simultaneous assignment is non-negotiable.

m6-t4.question: Why must decision rules be written BEFORE the data arrive?
options: Because platforms require it
To prevent panic-scaling on a good day and sunk-cost patience on a bad one
So clients cannot argue later
Because GA4 deletes old data
m6-t4.explanation: E.g., 'CPA < ₹150 for two weeks → scale +20%; CPA > ₹300 for three days → pause and diagnose' — thresholds set in advance remove emotion.

questions.question: A monthly report shows reach up 300% and enquiries down 25%. What is the professionally correct interpretation?
options: The campaign is succeeding; enquiries will follow next month
A vanity metric rose while a decision metric fell — diagnose the funnel: where exactly are enquiries lost between reach and conversion?
Analytics tools are unreliable
Increase the posting frequency to fix enquiries
questions.explanation: When applause metrics and business metrics diverge, the business metric wins — walk the KPI tree to find the broken branch.

questions.question: GA4 shows form_submit at 3% from social but 11% from organic search. Social volume is 10× larger. What should you check before cutting social?
options: Nothing — 3% justifies cutting social immediately
Assisted conversions and incrementality: social may be the discovery touch that feeds the organic searches, and last-click may be starving it
Whether the social posts used enough hashtags
The bounce rate of the homepage
questions.explanation: Channel-level last-click rates hide upstream discovery roles — model comparison or a geo/pause test before firing a channel.

questions.question: A stakeholder asks for 'a report with everything'. Applying this module, what do you deliver?
options: A 20-panel dashboard covering every available metric
The five-panel dashboard: header KPIs vs previous period, trend with target line, channel breakdown, funnel, and three insight notes
A raw export of all GA4 events
A weekly email with screenshots from each platform
questions.explanation: Stakeholders want the KPI tree live, not a wall of charts; panels that provoke no decision get deleted.

questions.question: Your A/B test shows variant B at 52% vs A at 48% on 60 conversions total. A colleague wants to ship B. What is the correct response?
options: Ship B — 52% is higher
The sample is far too small; run to sufficiency (a significance calculator) before believing a 4-point gap
Ship A to be safe
Run both forever
questions.explanation: Small samples produce noise wearing the costume of insight; pre-compute required sample size and run to it.

questions.question: Retargeting ads show the best ROAS in the account. Why is this not automatically proof they deserve more budget?
options: Retargeting is banned in India
Retargeting converts people who were often returning anyway — the incrementality question decides, not the attributed ROAS
ROAS cannot be measured for retargeting
Retargeting only works for e-commerce
questions.explanation: High conversion rates on warm audiences may reflect selection, not causation — a pause test or geo split reveals the truth.

questions.question: A new GA4 property is installed on a client site by the developer. What is your first professional act?
options: Build a Looker Studio dashboard
Verify the installation in Realtime/DebugView and configure ONE key event proxying the business action
Create 40 conversions for completeness
Turn off enhanced measurement to save data
questions.explanation: Unverified installations do not exist; then one business-proxy conversion, then Search Console/Ads links, enhanced measurement stays on.

questions.question: Under last-click, brand search gets 40% of conversions. The team wants to double brand-search budget. What does this module caution?
options: Brand search is always worth doubling
Brand search conversions are often partly harvesting demand created elsewhere — check what drives the searches before crediting the channel
Brand search is a vanity metric
GA4 cannot track brand search
questions.explanation: Last-click rewards the bottom of the funnel; the harvest channel gets credit for seeds planted by discovery channels.

questions.question: Which monthly practice embodies the optimisation loop's budget discipline?
options: Move the entire budget to the current best channel
Reallocate 10–20% from worst to best CPA, keeping one experimental line item, all logged
Keep budgets frozen for a quarter regardless of results
Spend equally on all channels for fairness
questions.explanation: Small, continuous, documented reallocation — the 70/20/10 discipline from Lesson 4.4 applied monthly — beats wholesale bets.

questions.question: The 'how did you hear about us?' log at every order is valuable because it:
options: Is required by GA4
Provides model-free, consent-safe attribution evidence that triangulates platform claims
Replaces the need for a website
Automatically improves ad targeting
questions.explanation: The unglamorous truth-teller: free of attribution-model bias, it grounds every dashboard's channel story.

questions.question: A dashboard blend of GA4 + Google Ads + a manual sheet broke after a platform field rename. What does the lesson recommend instead?
options: Rebuild the blend with more joins
Side-by-side panels per source, with the manual sheet as its own data source — no cross-connector joins
Abandon dashboards and use spreadsheets only
Screenshot the platforms weekly
questions.explanation: Blends break silently; adjacent panels deliver the same insight without the fragility — the manual layer stays first-class.
